title: Terminate owned transport groups after failed channel close
body:
UrlProtocol's host shutdown must complete even when a full native event-loop queue rejects close work, as required by https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/UrlProtocol/pull/992. This PR supplies the owned transport shutdown and dial-completion ordering needed for that change: a logically closed UDP parent can still have its port bound until the selector releases it. The final review work also fixes two demonstrated completion/error-ownership bugs in this shutdown path.

TCP and WebSocket terminate their owned acceptor groups after channel close settles, including failed close. QUIC retains owned outbound UDP parents through physical close and selector release, then terminates its owned worker group even after cleanup fails. Caller future changes cannot cancel cleanup. A normally returning callback that closes its connection keeps a successful dial pending until parent cleanup finishes; a rejected close that leaves a parent open reports its error without waiting for release that has not begun.

The consumer test `testHostStopDoesNotMutatePublishedListenerFailures` exposed a failure object being changed after public `unlisten()` had returned it. Multiple distinct close failures now use an aggregation-owned error: its cause retains the first original error and suppressed entries retain later errors. Single failures keep their original identity; no previously returned error is changed. Consumer evidence: https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/UrlProtocol/blob/wip/FLIBP13-evidence-20261114/evidence/FLIBP13/open-native-listener-row.md . The library's two-listener public regression has one red, one green and one reverted-red, without retries.

The G4 test then exposed a held physical-close promise completing after its event loop had terminated: its existing completion listener could no longer be dispatched, leaving the dial pending. Library-owned close promises now deliver their result without requiring another loop notification; actual channel work still follows the channel pipeline. The exact public shutdown-hook test fails on the prior head, passes with the change, and fails when only this promise change is reverted.

## Five review findings and final states

Prior finding table and reviews: https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/tree/wip/F93l-evidence-20261114/evidence/F93l , https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/blob/fa76029f389124d7ab8c0be7d22e74cc7f822f8a/evidence/R93T2/findings.md and https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/blob/5ae3865dd6624b7212b20577211ca65af0f62c84/evidence/R93A2/findings.md . Final proofs, source controls and reviews: https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/tree/wip/F93m-evidence-20261114/evidence/F93m .

- **G2 — closed:** `F93jQuicReleaseReentryTest` holds B publication after B cleanup starts from A's release callback and requires both exact UDP ports to rebind. F93l proof: red 0/1, green 1/1, reverted-red 0/1, one attempt each; source unchanged in F93m.
- **G3 — not closable without an API change:** `QuicTransport.kt:53-56,78-81` has no selector/provider dependency parameter; `DatagramPortRelease.kt:63-67` privately creates the system NIO handler. A caller cannot force the post-capture supplier at `:40-45` to fail without internal access or process-global replacement. No visibility expansion or internal-helper test was added.
- **G4 — product defect fixed, full public condition proven:** `F93mQuicDestroyedLoopReleaseTest` uses the established ECDSA route, held original close promises and a public zero-quiet-period shutdown hook. Two releases are pending before destruction with no selector pass; a third registers during completion and a fourth after termination. The no-terminal-drain control fails at the first waiter. Original head fails at the fourth waiter; fixed head passes 1/1 and reverting only promise delivery fails 0/1 at that fourth waiter. Each is one attempt, retries/skips 0. All four exact UDP ports rebind in the passing case.
- **G6 — not closable without an API change:** private child completion at `QuicTransport.kt:331-341` registers/assigns the child at `:342-347` before the earliest public callback at `:361-374`. The constructor exposes no child/bootstrap dependency. Public callbacks can hold an already registered child or queued bind, neither forcing late attachment across close's inventory at `:157-165`.
- **G7 — native-resource proof retained; Java-history bound not closable without an API change:** `F93jQuicFailedDialResourceTest` retains warmup plus 128 measured failures, all 129 exact failure identities and close counts, later successful probes, physical closure, exact rebinds and descriptor-return checks. F93l red/green/reverted-red was 0/1,1/1,0/1. F93m changes only where that test observes the now-owned aggregate and adds an unchanged-visitor-error assertion. The contract retains original failed-close identities (`QuicTransport.kt:304-318,642-648,198-204`); no public retained-history bound/configuration or measurement distinguishes retained owner graphs from required error identities. Descriptor counts are not presented as proof of bounded Java history.

## Existing tests and binding rulings

F93m edits **zero default-branch tests**. Seven tests added by this PR change expected values in dedicated commits because multiple failures now use an owned aggregate:

- `F93bQuicSecondaryCloseFailureTest`: child identity moves from the result root to its cause; parent identity moves from the child's suppressed list to the aggregate's. It also checks the full aggregate message and unchanged child error.
- `F93cQuicMultipleCloseFailuresTest`: the first child remains the aggregate's cause; repeated shutdown retains the exact aggregate; all eight original errors remain in the graph and unchanged.
- `F93hQuicDatagramReleaseTest` and `R93ARejectedOpenParentDialTest`: visitor identity moves to the aggregate cause, parent-close identity to its suppressed entry; visitor suppressed state must stay empty.
- `F93jQuicFailedDialResourceTest`: the same aggregate observation correction applies to all 129 failures, with every resource/workload assertion preserved and an added unchanged-visitor assertion.
- `QuicTransportFailedDatagramCloseTest`: the two-error branch checks the original child under the aggregate; the single-error branch still requires the original root identity.
- `F93bRepeatedQuicShutdownFailureTest`: the same two-error correction retains the original child under the aggregate; repeated shutdown must still return the exact same aggregate, with every physical-cleanup assertion preserved. The first touched-class gate exposed this remaining old expectation (63/64 passed); its corrected two-case targeted register passes 2/2 without retry.

No existing assertion, timeout or iteration count was weakened or removed. Formatting also reordered one import in the new published-failure test.

The earlier 2026-11-09 17:03 UTC ruling permits retained-error assertions only in three approved scenarios against their own failures. F93l restored each original joint 10-second host-cleanup deadline: `ParentCloseOwnershipTest.failedCloseIsReturnedToEveryOwnerWithoutAnotherRequest`, `ConnectionCloseRetryTest.transportOwnedFailureCanBeRetriedWithoutChangingOrdinaryResult` and `ConnectionCloseRetryTest.concurrentRetriesShareHeldAttemptAndIsolateCallerFutureChanges`. The latter two retain their 5-second client bound and give the server only the remainder of the joint deadline. Shared helper behavior remains concurrent successful stops within 10 seconds; the two added transport-close identity checks remain. F93l proof was 0/3 red, 3/3 green, 0/3 reverted-red, one attempt each. These three cleanup edits are unchanged in F93m.

## Found while testing, not part of this change

The transport's Ed25519 certificate factory fails a minimal public connection attempt between two isolated hosts on **both develop and the PR runtime**: develop 0/1, head 0/1, exactly one body attempt each, no retries/skips. Both fail at the public connection wait and record a native certificate callback failure. This is inherited; no Ed25519 product fix or workaround is included here.

The exact dependencies are `io.netty:netty-codec-classes-quic:4.2.10.Final` and `io.netty:netty-codec-native-quic:4.2.10.Final:linux-x86_64`. Native default certificate mappings cover RSA and EC families but no Ed25519 mapping. Production callers of this factory in this repository: 0; README recommendations: 0. The interop caller uses ECDSA. Source hashes, locations, both single-attempt results and the minimal host test: https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/blob/wip/F93m-evidence-20261114/evidence/F93m/ed-classification.md . Identity-key examples are distinct from this certificate factory.

## Base and verification

Fresh clone verified OPEN at starting head https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/commit/540d17af7343e709fcbf42d67ac6da81f179efd0 . Develop https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/commit/e7c79098db289f6a08c8dd467f4bedeb4fd7d168 is already its ancestor; repeated fetch/rebase found 0 newer base commits and 0 equivalent fixes superseding this slice. Its Yamux accounting change does not change these transport paths.

A1 proof: 0/1 red, 1/1 green, 0/1 reverted-red; neighbors 10/10. G4 new-defect proof: 0/1 head red, 1/1 fixed green, 0/1 promise reverted-red, plus the separate 0/1 no-terminal-drain control. All valid proofs use single attempts with zero retries/skips. Early fixture construction/compile errors reached zero target assertions and are separately recorded, not counted as proof. Dedicated test and adversarial self-reviews read CODE_REVIEW.md, TESTING.md and PHILOSOPHY.md in full; no extra model was used.

Final product head: https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/commit/b3fa50420fe578cfa17abef8342f75f6592ce12d . All 39 touched classes passed **64/64**, exactly 64 first attempts, zero failures/errors/skips/retry entries, in one final Gradle --no-daemon run; local spotlessCheck also passed. The earlier pre-correction gate was 63/64 and exposed the seventh expected-value correction described above; its two-case targeted check passed 2/2 before this final run.

The `documentation` job on interim head a32b7345 failed only the new A1 test's import order: https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/actions/runs/43574153552/job/132384615265 . The formatting correction is included in the final head and its local spotlessCheck passes; no documentation/API-signature defect was reported by that job. Initial-head native Actions https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/actions/runs/43570021988 succeeded on workflow attempt 1: 1715/1717 first-attempt passes, 2 existing skips (`EchoSampleTest.connect1`, `QuicServerTestJava.checkConnectionIsNotClosedByTimeout`), retries none. Final-head Actions will be recorded after push; informational remote checks are not the campaign gate. No suite/check was re-requested, no remote run was submitted, and no merge, enqueue, publication or deployment was performed.

Final-head native Actions https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/actions/runs/43575715930 and documentation https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/actions/runs/43575715998 are pending on workflow attempt 1 at the 08:25 UTC read; the native run has no result artifacts yet, so final-head Actions case/retry counts are unavailable. The requested local/proof/classification bar is met and no further CI wait is performed.

An earlier TCP setup failure at https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/commit/68c436af remains unclassified; newer UDP results do not establish its mechanism or claim it fixed.

### Third review: restore held and reentrant close ordering

The third review found that F93m's immediate close-promise notification could put a close result before an earlier physical-close listener while the channel loop was still running. This contradicted the existing reentrant-close contract in README.md and could affect UrlProtocol host shutdown when a close callback requests another close.

The owned close promise now uses the channel loop's normal notification ordering and depth boundary. If that loop rejects a notification, the same notification runs directly, preserving completion after loop termination. Published failure aggregation, UDP port-release waits, owned-group cleanup and the three shared 10-second cleanup deadlines are unchanged.

- The reviewer's ordinary and reentrant held-close tests were added unchanged and each failed on its first attempt. Both pass with the fix and fail again with only the immediate-delivery implementation restored: ordering register 0/2, 2/2, 0/2; no retries or skips.
- F93mQuicDestroyedLoopReleaseTest passes with the fix and fails at the after-termination registration when only the earlier loop-bound promise implementation is restored: 1/1 green, 0/1 control, one attempt each. F93mPublishedCloseFailureTest also passes unchanged, 1/1.
- Final Gradle `--no-daemon` gate: 41 touched classes, 66/66 first-attempt passes, no failures, errors, skips or retry entries; `spotlessCheck` passes.
- The other immediate Netty promise at QuicTransport.kt:655 belongs only to private shutdown-hook cleanup. Its result reaches public shutdown after worker termination; it does not publish a separate close result that can overtake physical-close listeners. Seven other new CompletableFuture completion sites were also checked against their selection, destruction and termination barriers; none replaces a base-branch scheduled promise.
- Existing test edits in this lane: zero. A separate formatting commit changes whitespace only in the two newly added reviewer tests; their full tokens, including quoted strings, are identical before and after formatting. No default-branch test or assertion changes in this lane.
- Local full documentation verification requires Android SDK platform 30/build-tools 30.0.3, absent in this checkout's environment. Formatting passed, and the available documentation-laziness check passed 1/1 on its first attempt. The final-head [Documentation contract run](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/actions/runs/43582182505) and [native run](https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/actions/runs/43582182565) are pending on attempt 1; full Actions XML counts are not yet available.

Proofs, controls, formatting token comparison and the completion-site inventory: https://github.com/CodexCoder21Organization/jvm-libp2p/tree/wip/F93n-evidence-20261114/evidence/F93n . No publication, merge, queue entry or deployment was performed.
